<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

In Model Runner V2 verification, `_resample_kernel` now returns early for a vocab block whose target logits are all `-inf` (masked by top-k/top-p or a logits processor): the residual there is `-inf` too, so the draft-logit load and the Gumbel draw are skipped. Sampled tokens are bitwise identical. Part of the rejection-sampling work tracked in #61024; first of a stack (see the end of this description).

## Claims

- Resample kernel on top-p-masked verify rows (K = 3, top-p 0.95, Qwen3-0.6B logits, V = 151,936, GB300): **165.9 → 55.4 µs** (creative-writing rows) and **149.5 → 42.2 µs** (math rows) at 256 requests; 13.7 → 6.8 µs at 16 requests.
- No cost on unmasked rows: the check runs only when some request in the chunk may have masked logits (top-p = 1 rows stay at 165.1 µs; forcing the check on them would cost 173.7 µs, +5%).
- Output is bitwise identical with the skip on or off.

## Validation

```
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/spec_decode/test_rejection_sampler_utils.py \
    tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_sampler_flags.py tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_rejection_sampler_chunking.py -q
# 127 passed (GB300). Unmodified main, first two files: 111 passed; this adds 4 parametrizations.
```

- `test_skip_masked_vocab_blocks_is_bitwise_identical`: two whole vocab blocks and most of a third masked, with and without draft logits, fp32 and fp64 Gumbel; skip on vs off must match bitwise.
- `test_logits_processing_cache_matches_request_features` gains the expected `may_mask_logits` per request feature; temperature-only is the case that needs processing but never masks.

Kernel times: `_resample_kernel` device time from the torch profiler (10 calls after 3 warm-up), the same inputs through upstream `main` and this branch, loaded side by side; outputs compared on the valid positions only.

| rows (requests × 4) | profile | top-p | main µs | skip on µs |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 64 | creative | 0.95 | 13.7 | 6.8 |
| 1,024 | creative | 0.95 | 165.9 | 55.4 |
| 1,024 | math | 0.95 | 149.5 | 42.2 |
| 1,024 | creative | 1.0 | 165.1 | 165.1 (gated off) |

Not measured: end-to-end serving throughput. In a verify-step harness with vLLM's own chain (fp32 copy, temperature, Triton top-p mask, rejection sampling) the same kernel change took a 256-request step from 2,086 to 1,976 µs.

## Details

- **Gate.** The block max costs about 5% of the kernel when nothing is masked, so `rejection_sample` takes `skip_masked_vocab_blocks` (default off) and `RejectionSampler._verify` turns it on when any request in the chunk may have masked logits. `Sampler` records that per request in `may_mask_logits`: min-p, top-k or top-p active, or thinking-budget forcing or a logits processor (counted conservatively, e.g. logit bias). Temperature alone only scales and never sets the flag. No host/device sync: the flag is a NumPy lookup.
- **Why it is exact.** The residual is a subset of the target's support, so an all-`-inf` target block yields an all-`-inf` residual. Such a block never wins the global argmax unless every block is `-inf`, and in that case it reports index 0, which is what the argmax of an all-`-inf` block returns.
- **Not duplicating.** Searched open PRs for "resample kernel skip", "rejection sampler resample", "top-p rejection sampling" and #61024: #41258 (lazy recovery) changes the V1 sampler, #48928 (FlashInfer AIR top-p) replaces the mask itself; neither touches the MRV2 resample kernel.
- **With the on-load path.** #65102 and #65103 carry this commit. There the kernels apply the top-p cutoff to raw logits as they load them, so the raw block is never all `-inf`; their next commit tests the block after the cutoff instead, which is the same tensor on this PR's path.
- **Stack.** 1/4, independent of the rest: (2) #65101 `topp_cutoffs_lse` op, (3) #65102 top-p applied as target logits load, (4) #65103 target log-sum-exp from that op. #65104 (draft log-sum-exp from the drafter) closed: a net loss once the drafter's cost is counted.

AI assistance (Claude) was used to write this change and its tests; the submitter is reviewing every line.

---

+def test_skip_masked_vocab_blocks_is_bitwise_identical(
+    has_draft_logits: bool, use_fp64: bool
+):
+    """skip_masked_vocab_blocks lets the resample kernel skip vocab blocks whose
+    target logits are all -inf (e.g. masked by top-k/top-p). The sampled tokens
+    must match the unskipped path exactly.
+    """
+    torch.manual_seed(0)
+    device = "cuda"
+    K = 3
+    vocab_size = 4 * 8192
+    target_logits_1d = torch.randn(vocab_size, device=device)
+    target_logits_1d[8192 : 3 * 8192] = float("-inf")  # two whole blocks
+    target_logits_1d[3 * 8192 + 100 :] = float("-inf")  # most of the last one
+    draft_logits_1d = torch.randn(vocab_size, device=device)
+    inputs = _build_rejection_sample_inputs(
+        target_logits_1d, draft_logits_1d, K, temperature=1.0, num_trials=256
+    )
+    if not has_draft_logits:
+        inputs["draft_logits"] = None
+
+    def run(skip: bool) -> tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]:
+        return _rejection_sample(
+            **inputs,
+            num_speculative_steps=K,
+            use_fp64=use_fp64,
+            skip_masked_vocab_blocks=skip,
+        )
+
+    ref_sampled, ref_num_sampled = run(False)
+    sampled, num_sampled = run(True)
+
+    torch.testing.assert_close(num_sampled, ref_num_sampled, rtol=0, atol=0)
+    valid = torch.arange(K + 1, device=device) < num_sampled.unsqueeze(1)
+    torch.testing.assert_close(sampled[valid], ref_sampled[valid], rtol=0, atol=0)
+
